🎤 Examiner Viva Defense Cheat-Sheet (Key Questions & Answers)

Also available in docs/VIVA_DEFENSE_GUIDE.md & docs/IEEE_PROJECT_REPORT.md
Examiner Question Core Technical Answer & Where to Point in Code
1. Where is the Adaptive Software Engineering (ASE) part? Point to Components #5 (Runtime Monitoring), #6 (SLA Manager), #7 (MAPE-K Engine), #8 (Adaptive Model Selector), #9 (Stability & Hysteresis Manager), #10 (Model Switching Manager), and #11 (Knowledge Base). Together they form a closed self-adaptive feedback loop.
2. Why doesn't the system switch on temporary spikes (`90 → 105 → 98 → 103 → 95 ms`)? In c09_stability_hysteresis.py, we enforce a Persistent Violation Window (`N = 5` consecutive breaches). When latency drops back to `98 ms` on the next tick, the breach counter resets to `0` and logs TRANSIENT_FLUCTUATION_ABSORBED.
3. Why choose Random Forest (`60ms`) instead of Logistic Regression (`20ms`) during high load? In c08_model_selector.py, candidates violating hard SLA constraints are filtered out first. Logistic Regression has 82% accuracy, violating our Accuracy SLA (`≥ 85%`). Random Forest achieves 88% accuracy and ~65ms latency, satisfying all SLAs.
4. How do you prevent model oscillation (thrashing) when load cools down? Our Bidirectional Hysteresis rule in c09_stability_hysteresis.py requires: (1) post-switch cooldown expiry, (2) 5 consecutive stable ticks, and (3) projected XGBoost latency ≤ SLA - Hysteresis Margin (100 - 12 = 88 ms) before switching back.
